correctness.rationale: For a simple constrained target eigenvalue, the Schur complement is analytic in inverse penalty near zero and has a simple characteristic root. Expanding the effective operator gives the explicit second coefficient, while Hermite interpolation of the analytic branch together with the Hellmann-Feynman derivative gives the stated order-2p extrapolation. Exact and reproducible numerical checks support the algebra.

originality.rationale: The primary source gives the first-order coefficient, value-only two-level second-order extrapolation, and Hellmann-Feynman sensitivity, but not the explicit second coefficient or derivative-enhanced fourth-/higher-order formulas. Generic Richardson and Hermite extrapolation are classical and are not claimed as new. Searches found no prior application yielding these formulas for this projected-Hessian penalty path; originality is only to the best of our knowledge.

value.rationale: The result extracts twice the asymptotic order per penalty level when derivative data already available from the penalized eigenpair are retained, potentially reducing the penalty magnitude needed for a target asymptotic accuracy while also supplying an explicit next-order error coefficient.
